source_text:
Ἐπλήγησαν τὰς ψυχὰς οἱ ἄνθρωποι καὶ πρὸς τὴν 9.122 ἀκοὴν
ἀπεπάγησαν τοὺς ἅλας καὶ τὴν τράπεζαν αἰδεσθέντες καὶ τὸν ἐν πενίᾳ φιλότιμον
ἑστιάτορα. Ὁ δὲ καὶ ἔτι παρεκάλει πρὸς τὴν τόλμαν τῆς ἀναιρέσεως καὶ μηδὲ πρὸς
ὀλίγον διστάζειν ἐπεκελεύετο λέγων ὡς οὐ τῆς ἐκείνων χειρὸς ὁ φόνος, ἀλλὰ τῶν
προσταξάντων ἡ ἐπιχείρησις. Εἶπεν, ἔπεισεν, ἔπαθε καὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν ἀποτμηθεὶς
ἱερεῖον τῷ Θεῷ κεχαρισμένον προσήχθη. Στύλον καὶ ἔρεισμα τῶν θείων τῆς
οἰκουμένης ἐκκλησιῶν, ἐξ ἐκείνου μέχρι τοῦ νῦν τοῦτον ἔχομεν, ἄνθρωποι· καὶ
μαρτύρων ἐστὶν οὗτος περιφανέστατος ἐν τοῖς ἀρίστοις ἔχων αὐτὸς τὸ πρωτεῖον.
Οὗτος ἐφέλκεται πανδημεὶ πάντας πρὸς τὸ ἑαυτοῦ καταγώγιον· καὶ πληρεῖς αἱ
λεωφόροι τῶν ἀφ' ἑκάστης χώρας πρὸς τὸν τόπον ἐπειγομένων τῆς προσευχῆς. Ἔστι
μὲν οὖν ὁ μεγαλοπρεπὴς ἐκεῖνος ναός, ὃς καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν ἔχειν τοῦ μάρτυρος ἐκληρώθη
σῶμα, θλιβομένων ἄνεσις, κακου μένων ἰατρεῖον, λιμωττόντων τράπεζα.
∆αψιλέστερον γὰρ τρέφει Φωκᾶς νῦν τελευτήσας ἤπερ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ ζῶν Ἰωσὴφ τὸ
πρότερον. Ἐκεῖνος μὲν γὰρ ἀργυρίου τὸν σῖτον διήμειβεν, οὗτος δὲ προῖκα τοῖς
δεομένοις χαρίζεται. Οὕτω πτωχῶν καὶ ἀλητευόντων φῦλα προστρέχει τῷ τῆς
Σινώπης ἰσθμῷ καθάπερ τινὶ κοινῷ ταμιείῳ. Ἀλλ' ἐκεῖ μὲν οὕτως. Εἰ δέ που καὶ
ἀλλαχοῦ διὰ μικρῶν λειψάνων οἷον ἀποικίαν τινὰ μητροπόλεως ὁ μάρτυς ἑαυτῷ
κατεστήσατο, θαυμαστὸς καὶ οὗτος ὁ τόπος καὶ πᾶσι χριστιανοῖς περισπούδαστος,
ὥσπερ δὴ καὶ οὗτος ὁ παρ' ἡμῖν ἱερὸς χωρὸς κατα γώγιον ἑορταζόντων ἐστί. Τίμιος
2
γὰρ ἐναντίον Κυρίου ὁ θάνατος τῶν ὁσίων αὐτοῦ· καὶ πολλαχοῦ μερισθέντα τὰ
λείψανα ὁλόκληρον πανταχοῦ τῷ τρισμακαρίῳ σώζει τὴν εὐφημίαν. Οὕτω γοῦν καὶ
κατὰ τὴν βασιλεύουσαν πόλιν, τὴν κορυφὴν Ἰταλίας καὶ βασιλίδα τοῦ κόσμου, ἔστι
τῷ μάρτυρι δορυφορία πάνδημος καὶ τιμή, οἶκος τε περιφανής, ἠσκημένος εἰς
κάλλος. Οὐχ ἧττον δὲ Ῥωμαῖοι τὸν Φωκᾶν θεραπεύουσιν ἢ Πέτρον καὶ Παῦλον. ∆ιὸ
καί, ὡς ὁ λόγος διδάσκει, τὴν κεφαλὴν τοῦ μάρτυρος ἐσπουδασμένως ἐκτήσαντο
ἀντίστροφον τῆς μιαρᾶς Ἡρωδιάδος ἑλόμενοι γνώμην. Ἡ μὲν γὰρ αἵματος διψῶσα
9.124 δικαίου, κεφαλὴν τιμίαν εἰς ὕβριν ἐξῄτησεν· οἱ δέ, τιμῆς χάριν καὶ ὠφελείας
τῆς ἑαυτῶν, μαρτυρικὴν ἀξίως κεφαλὴν περιεποιήσαντο. Ναῦται δὲ καὶ πλωτῆρες οἱ
πανταχοῦ, οὐχ οἱ τὸν Εὔξεινον διαπλέοντες πόντον, ἀλλὰ καὶ οἱ τὸν Ἀδρίαν
τέμνοντες καὶ ὑπὲρ Αἰγαίου φερόμενοι καὶ ὅσοι τὸν ὠκεανὸν πλέουσι τὸν ἑσπέριον
καὶ τοῖς ἐῴοις κόλποις ἐνθαλαττεύουσι, τὰ συνήθη κελεύσματα οἷς τοῦ πλοῦ πόνον
προσανα παύουσιν, εἰς καινὴν τοῦ μάρτυρος μετέβαλον εὐφημίαν· καὶ διὰ γλώσσης
ἐστὶν ὅλως ὁ Φωκᾶς αὐτοῖς ὑπᾳδόμενος, ἐπεὶ καὶ ἐναργῆ παρέχει τῆς βοηθείας τὰ
σύμβολα. Πολλάκις γὰρ ὤφθη, νῦν μὲν νύκτωρ προσδοκωμένου χειμῶνος διεγείρων
τὸν κυβερνήτην τῷ πηδαλίῳ ἐπινυστάξαντα· ἄλλοτε δὲ πάλιν τοὺς κάλως διατείνων
καὶ τῆς ὀθόνης ἐπιμελούμενος καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς πρώρας προοπτεύων τὰ βράχη.
orientation: Asterius is preaching about the martyr Phocas, and has just narrated how Phocas revealed himself to the soldiers sent to kill him.
pass_a_gloss: The men were struck in their souls and at the hearing they were frozen, reverencing the salt and the table and the host generous in poverty. But he still kept urging them toward the boldness of the killing and commanded them not to hesitate even a little, saying that the murder was not of their hand, but the undertaking of those who commanded it. He spoke, he persuaded, he suffered, and having been beheaded he was offered as a sacrifice pleasing to God. A pillar and support of the divine churches of the inhabited world, from that time until now we have this man, O people; and of martyrs this one is most illustrious, having himself the first place among the best. This one draws all people in a body to his own lodging; and the highways are full of those hastening from each land to the place of prayer. That magnificent church, which was allotted to have the holy body of the martyr, is relief of the afflicted, a hospital of the sick, a table of the hungry. For Phocas now that he has died feeds more abundantly than Joseph formerly when living in Egypt. For that one exchanged the grain for silver, but this one gives freely to those in need. Thus tribes of the poor and wanderers run to the isthmus of Sinope as to some common storehouse. But there it is so. And if somewhere also elsewhere through small relics the martyr established for himself a kind of colony of a mother city, this place too is wondrous and much sought after by all Christians, just as indeed this holy place among us is a lodging of those celebrating. For precious before the Lord is the death of his holy ones; and the relics divided in many places preserve everywhere whole the good fame of the thrice-blessed one. Thus indeed also in the reigning city, the summit of Italy and queen of the world, there is for the martyr a public bodyguard and honor, and a conspicuous house, adorned for beauty. And no less do the Romans honor Phocas than Peter and Paul. Therefore also, as the account teaches, they eagerly acquired the head of the martyr, choosing a judgment opposite to that of the abominable Herodias. For she, thirsting for righteous blood, demanded a precious head for insult; but they, for the sake of honor and their own benefit, worthily secured the martyric head. And sailors and voyagers everywhere, not those sailing across the Euxine sea, but also those cutting the Adriatic and carried over the Aegean and as many as sail the western ocean and voyage in the eastern gulfs, changed the customary commands with which they relieve the toil of the voyage into a new praise of the martyr; and Phocas is altogether on their tongue being sung, since he also provides clear signs of his help. For often he was seen, now at night when a storm was expected waking the helmsman who had nodded off at the rudder; and at another time again stretching the ropes and caring for the sail and from the prow watching ahead for the reefs.

choices.english: he was offered as a sacrifice pleasing to God
choices.why: ἱερεῖον is a sacrificial victim; κεχαρισμένον means pleasing or acceptable; προσήχθη is passive 'was brought/offered'
rejected: he was brought as a gift acceptable to God
he was led as a victim

choices.why: στύλος is pillar, ἔρεισμα is support/prop; both are architectural metaphors for Phocas's role in the churches
πανδημεί means 'with the whole people, en masse'; πάντας is 'all'; the redundancy is emphatic
per glossary, καταγώγιον is rendered 'lodging'; here it refers to the martyr's shrine as a place of refuge
δορυφορία is a bodyguard or escort of honor; πάνδημος is public, of all the people

choices.term: ἀντίστροφον τῆς μιαρᾶς Ἡρωδιάδος ἑλόμενοι γνώμην
choices.english: choosing a judgment opposite to that of the abominable Herodias
choices.why: ἀντίστροφον means 'turned opposite, corresponding in reverse'; γνώμην is judgment or intention; the Romans' choice is the reverse of Herodias's
rejected: taking a decision contrary to the abominable Herodias
adopting a mind opposite to that of the foul Herodias

bible_refs.note: Τίμιος ἐναντίον Κυρίου ὁ θάνατος τῶν ὁσίων αὐτοῦ (Precious before the Lord is the death of his holy ones); Septuagint Psalm 115:6

pass_b_english: The men were struck in their souls and froze at what they heard, reverencing the salt and the table and the host who showed such generosity in poverty. But he kept urging them to dare the killing and commanded them not to hesitate even a little, saying that the murder was not the work of their hands but the undertaking of those who had given the orders. He spoke, he persuaded, he suffered, and when his head was cut off he was offered as a sacrifice pleasing to God. From that time until now, we have him as a pillar and support of the divine churches throughout the world, and among the best of the martyrs he is the most illustrious, holding first place himself. He draws all people in a body to his lodging, and the highways are full of those hurrying from every country to the place of prayer. That magnificent church, which was allotted to hold the martyr's sacred body, is relief for the oppressed, a hospital for the afflicted, a table for the hungry. For Phocas now that he has died feeds more generously than Joseph did long ago while living in Egypt. Joseph exchanged grain for silver, but Phocas gives freely to those in need. So tribes of the poor and wandering run to the isthmus of Sinope as to a common storehouse. That is how it is there. And if somewhere else the martyr has established for himself through small relics a kind of colony of the mother city, that place too is wondrous and eagerly sought by all Christians, just as this sacred place among us is a lodging for those who celebrate. Precious before the Lord is the death of his holy ones (Psalm 116:15), and though the relics have been divided in many places, they preserve the martyr's complete renown everywhere. So too in the imperial city, the crown of Italy and queen of the world, the martyr has a public bodyguard and honor, and a splendid house adorned for beauty. The Romans honor Phocas no less than Peter and Paul. Therefore, as the account teaches, they eagerly acquired the martyr's head, choosing a judgment opposite to that of the abominable Herodias. She thirsted for righteous blood and demanded a precious head for insult, but they, for the sake of honor and their own benefit, worthily secured a martyr's head. Sailors and seafarers everywhere—not only those who cross the Black Sea, but also those who cut through the Adriatic Sea and are carried over the Aegean Sea, and all who sail the Atlantic Ocean and make their way among the eastern gulfs—have turned the customary chants with which they ease the labor of the voyage into a new praise of the martyr. Phocas is always on their lips in song, since he also gives clear signs of his help. For he has often been seen, now at night when a storm was expected, waking the helmsman who had nodded off at the rudder; at other times stretching the ropes and tending the sail and watching from the prow for the reefs.
notes: The source text contains a line break and page number 9.122 embedded in the first sentence; no text appears to be missing.
The phrase 'κακου μένων' appears to be a typographical split of 'κακουμένων' (those afflicted/being ill-treated) across a line break; glossed as 'the sick' in context of ἰατρεῖον.
The phrase 'κατα γώγιον' is split across a line break; it is the single word καταγώγιον.

last_rejected.why: ἰατρεῖον means 'healing place/physician's office', not modern 'hospital'
last_rejected.fix: a clinic for the suffering, or a place of healing for the afflicted
last_rejected.ruling: ἰατρεῖον denotes a place of healing; 'hospital' is a standard acceptable rendering, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: δορυφορία here means retinue/attendant honor guard, not protective 'bodyguard'
last_rejected.ruling: δορυφορία means escort/retinue; 'bodyguard' conveys attendant honor, not a misleading meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: choosing a judgment opposite to that of the abominable Herodias
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀντίστροφον τῆς μιαρᾶς Ἡρωδιάδος ἑλόμενοι γνώμην
last_rejected.why: γνώμην is 'purpose/intent', not 'judgment'; they chose an opposite purpose
last_rejected.fix: choosing a purpose opposite to that of the abominable Herodias
last_rejected.ruling: γνώμην spans judgment, purpose, intent; 'judgment' fits the Herodias contrast and is within normal range.
